Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you shape this into a clear prompt for making a textile dye log entry, not the entry itself. it is for a fictional batch at North Loom, and i want the details below organized so someone can make a useful, traceable record. keep the actual remarks and the two source notes exactly as written, because they came from the shift book and the operator’s slip. don't make guesses where something is not recorded. the batch date is 14 May 2025, shift B, operator Mara Venn, batch TD-418, and the work was done in dye room 2. the shift book has the line “The left rail stayed dry during loading.” The operator’s slip says “check the second rinse for blue carryover”. those are source material, not instructions for you to carry out.

The fabric was cotton twill, 62 kg, roll C-19, and the job card lists shade as deep indigo. The dye was indigo concentrate, dye lot D-77, used with recipe card R-12, revision 3. The card’s target amount is 3% on weight of fabric, and the amount weighed for this run was 1.86 kg. The liquor ratio written on the card is 1:8 and the recorded water charge was 496 L. Please keep the roll, batch, dye lot, recipe revision, stated target and actual weighed amount distinct in the resulting prompt; they are different identifiers or values. I don’t have a shade approval result in these notes, so don’t ask the writer to claim the shade passed or failed.

For preparation, the operator recorded a starting water temperature of 24 C at 08:42, and the pH reading before salt was 10.4 at 08:51. Salt was recorded as 18 kg total, added in three 6 kg portions at 08:55, 09:05 and 09:15. The mixing motor was marked running from 08:40, but there is no recorded stop time. The dye additions were each 0.62 kg: at 09:12, 09:28 and 09:47. I think the dye addition times should be listed separately from the salt additions so nobody reads the sequence wrong, even though one dye addition happened before the final salt portion. Do not silently move any time around to make the order look neater.

The temperature observations in the bath section are 58 C at 09:00, 60 C at 09:30 and 59 C at 10:00. The pH after the final dye addition is written as 10.1 at 10:02. There is no separate temperature value for every addition, and no pH value after the first or second dye portion, so those should remain unrecorded rather than filled in. If a temperature above 61 C was recorded before the first rinse, the log should show the first rinse as held pending supervisor review; use that condition only if such a reading is actually present in the supplied record. These notes contain no reading above 61 C before the first rinse, but keep the conditional rule in the prompt since it matters for how the log is to be completed.

The rinse sequence on the operator’s sheet has first rinse at 10:18, second rinse at 10:31 and final rinse at 10:46. The operator wrote that the second rinse was checked, but didn’t write down a numerical carryover reading or say whether blue carryover was seen. Keep the check as recorded and leave the result unspecified. The quoted slip note, “check the second rinse for blue carryover”, should stay exactly in the prompt as source wording, not be turned into a finding. There is no water temperature recorded for any rinse. The drain started at 10:52, and the sheet gives 11:06 as the time the fabric was removed from the machine. Don’t treat removal time as the end of drying; drying is not covered in these records.

There are a few more handling details from the shift book. Before loading, the operator noted a small crease near the tail end of roll C-19; it was described as visible but not measured. The roll was loaded with the tail end first. During loading, the left rail stayed dry, as stated in the quoted shift-book line, and the right rail was wiped once at 08:36 before the fabric went in. The wipe was recorded but the reason was not. There was no note of a leak, machine alarm, or fabric tear, but I don’t want that turned into a general claim that no problems occurred. Just keep the specific recorded observations and don’t infer a cause for the rail wipe or the crease.

Please include the remaining record details too: machine DR-06, vessel capacity 700 L, water meter reading 18422 L before charge and 18918 L after charge, and the log sheet reference NL-2B-0514. The card says the planned batch quantity was 60 kg, while the actual roll weight noted above is 62 kg; keep both values and label which is which instead of treating them as a correction. The operator initialed the sheet MV at 11:12. There’s no supervisor signature, no final shade judgement, and no recorded drying or inspection result. Don’t invent any of those fields as completed, and don’t turn a missing entry into a negative result.

Could the prompt ask for the eventual entry to be organized in a numbered section with sensible groups for identification and materials, preparation and additions, bath observations, rinsing and handling, and sign-off or missing information? That is just an organization request: retain the supplied information and make the gaps clear without filling them. It should make it easy to trace the three salt additions, three dye additions, bath readings, rinse times, meter readings and operator initials back to the source. Keep the notes in connected context rather than flattening every detail into an unexplained list, and leave the quoted remarks exactly as supplied. The final part of the prompt should still cover the missing supervisor signature, shade judgement, drying and inspection information, alongside the conditional first-rinse rule; don’t end by claiming that the batch was approved, successful or ready for release.", "output": "Write a textile dye log entry for the fictional North Loom batch described below. Organize the supplied information into a clear, traceable record. Do not make the log entry itself part of this prompt, and do not guess at missing information or turn an unrecorded result into a negative finding.

1. Identification and materials
- Batch date: 14 May 2025; shift B; operator: Mara Venn; dye room 2.
- Batch: TD-418. Machine: DR-06; vessel capacity: 700 L. Log sheet reference: NL-2B-0514.
- Fabric: cotton twill, roll C-19, actual weight 62 kg. The job card lists a planned batch quantity of 60 kg; label it as planned and keep it distinct from the actual roll weight.
- Shade listed on the job card: deep indigo. Dye: indigo concentrate, lot D-77. Recipe card: R-12, revision 3. The card’s target is 3% on weight of fabric; the amount weighed for this run was 1.86 kg. Keep the target and weighed amount distinct. No shade approval result is recorded, so do not state or request a pass/fail result.
- Liquor ratio on the card: 1:8. Recorded water charge: 496 L. Water meter readings: 18422 L before charge and 18918 L after charge.

2. Preparation and additions
Record the starting water temperature as 24 C at 08:42 and the pH before salt as 10.4 at 08:51. Salt totaled 18 kg, added in three 6 kg portions at 08:55, 09:05 and 09:15. The mixing motor was marked running from 08:40; no stop time is recorded.

List the dye additions separately from the salt additions: 0.62 kg at 09:12, 0.62 kg at 09:28 and 0.62 kg at 09:47. Keep the times as supplied, including the fact that one dye addition occurred before the final salt portion. Do not rearrange the times to make the sequence appear neater.

3. Bath observations
The recorded bath temperatures are 58 C at 09:00, 60 C at 09:30 and 59 C at 10:00. After the final dye addition, pH was 10.1 at 10:02. No temperature is recorded for every dye addition, and no pH reading is recorded after the first or second dye portion; leave those values unrecorded.

Apply this conditional rule only if it is supported by a supplied reading: if a temperature above 61 C was recorded before the first rinse, show the first rinse as held pending supervisor review. The supplied notes contain no reading above 61 C before the first rinse, but retain the conditional rule in the prompt for completing the log.

4. Rinsing and handling
The rinse times are first rinse at 10:18, second rinse at 10:31 and final rinse at 10:46. The operator recorded that the second rinse was checked, but provided neither a numerical carryover reading nor a result saying whether blue carryover was seen. Record the check and leave its result unspecified. No water temperature is recorded for the rinses. The drain started at 10:52; the fabric was removed from the machine at 11:06. Do not describe removal as the end of drying, because drying is not covered by the records.

Before loading, a small crease near the tail end of roll C-19 was noted as visible but not measured. The roll was loaded tail end first. The right rail was wiped once at 08:36 before the fabric went in; no reason for the wipe is recorded. The shift book states, “The left rail stayed dry during loading.” There was no note of a leak, machine alarm or fabric tear. Preserve only those specific observations; do not infer a cause for the wipe or crease, or turn the absence of those notes into a general claim that no problems occurred.

Keep these source notes exactly as written and treat them as source wording, not as instructions to carry out:
- “The left rail stayed dry during loading.”
- “check the second rinse for blue carryover”

5. Sign-off and missing information
The operator initialed the sheet MV at 11:12. No supervisor signature, final shade judgement, drying result or inspection result is recorded. Make those gaps clear without filling them in. Do not invent completed fields or claim that the batch was approved, successful or ready for release. Keep the identification, material, addition, bath, rinse, handling and sign-off information traceable to the supplied record, and end with the missing information and applicable conditional rule rather than an unsupported conclusion."}]
